subject.title: Decouple mode="session" from thread binding requirement

question: Should OpenClaw make non-thread persistent native and ACP `sessions_spawn` sessions a first-class supported contract, and what routing, lifecycle, and cleanup semantics should they use?
rationale: The source reproduction is clear, but the fix changes session ownership, message delivery, cleanup, label targeting, and ACP behavior rather than repairing a narrow implementation defect.

options.title: Define non-thread persistence
options.body: Approve a first-class unbound persistent-session contract and require one implementation that updates runtime, schema, docs, and tests together.

options.title: Keep session thread-bound
options.body: Leave `mode="session"` tied to channel thread binding and narrow follow-up work to docs and existing `mode="run"` or `sessions_send` guidance.

options.title: Split ACP and native designs
options.body: Handle ACP persistent affinity through a separate contract such as `affinityKey` or delegated workers while deciding native subagent persistence separately.

recommendation.title: Define non-thread persistence
recommendation.body: Approve a first-class unbound persistent-session contract and require one implementation that updates runtime, schema, docs, and tests together.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent core thread-binding refactor and active maintenance of the spawn/session area make this the best available routing owner for the product-contract decision.
